title: Conversational Session Contract Playbook
author: Priya Singh
body:
Summary

This playbook defines the product-level contract primitives, SLOs, billing mappings, and rollout guidance for Conversational Session Contracts (CSCs). CSCs are the canonical package that encapsulates per-session runtime guarantees, fidelity expectations, billing signals, and automated fallback policies for Redwood customers using conversational (chat/assistant) endpoints. The goal is to provide a predictable, auditable surface that aligns product, billing, and infra for low-friction migrations between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Goals

- Provide a small, composable set of session primitives that cover 90% of customer conversational use cases.
- Make fidelity & cost trade-offs explicit and machine-readable.
- Ensure safe rollouts with canarying, auto-fallback, and observability hooks.
- Align SLOs to billing to avoid surprise invoices while enabling predictable economics.

Scope

This playbook covers: session lifecycle, contract primitives, SLO targets and alerts, billing mapping, runtime enforcement strategy, developer ergonomics (API + SDK), and operations/runbook steps. It does NOT prescribe kernel-level serving implementation or third-party model licensing.

Definitions

- Session: A logical conversation with an ID and bounded TTL that aggregates requests and token usage for billing and fidelity purposes.
- Contract: The JSON-serializable object that customers pin to a session to express SLOs, fidelity budget, and fallback policies.
- Fidelity: The expected quality/per-token compute profile (e.g., high, medium, low) mapped to model/quantization pairs.
- Variant: A named model+config tuple (example: gptx-2-8q, llama-70b-fp16).

Contract primitives (stable API surface)

1) contract_id (string) — unique customer-visible ID.
2) session_ttl_ms (integer string) — how long the session ID is valid since the last activity. Default: "1800000" (30 minutes).
3) fidelity_budget (string) — token-budget or compute-budget per session. Format: "tokens:1000" or "compute:0.75".
4) slo_profile (string) — "interactive" | "transactional" | "batch-like". Each profile maps to latency and availability targets.
5) fallback_policy (string) — serialized policy with prioritized variants and cost thresholds.
6) billing_mode (string) — "per_token" | "per_session" | "hybrid".
7) telemetry_level (string) — "none" | "basic" | "detailed" (affects retention & cost).

Example contract (canonical)

{
  "contract_id": "acme-chat-basic-v1",
  "session_ttl_ms": "3600000",
  "fidelity_budget": "tokens:2000",
  "slo_profile": "interactive",
  "fallback_policy": "[\"gptx-3-8q\",\"gptx-2-8q\"]",
  "billing_mode": "hybrid",
  "telemetry_level": "basic"
}

SLOs and thresholds (product-aligned)

Table: Session SLO mapping (product surface)

| slo_profile | target_p50_ms | target_p95_ms | availability | error_budget/month | default_telemetry |
| interactive | 70 | 250 | 99.8% | 0.2% | basic |
| transactional | 150 | 500 | 99.5% | 0.5% | detailed |
| batch-like | 500 | 1500 | 99.0% | 1.0% | detailed |

Notes:
- p50/p95 are measured per single-turn token generation latency (end-to-end) excluding client-side network.
- Availability = fraction of successful responses not hitting hard-fallback (400/5xx excluded).
- Error budget is applied to the contract_id at tenant level and can be traded for credits (see Billing mapping).

Billing mapping & pricing primitives

- per_token: bill raw generation tokens by model variant rate. Session contracts can define a cursor threshold after which a lower-cost variant is eligible.
- per_session: a flat rate per session start; suitable for short interactions or high-variance token usage.
- hybrid: baseline per_session + marginal per_token above the session token floor.

Default recommended price bands (internal product guidance only):

- interactive/hybrid baseline: $0.003 per session start + per_token at variant rate after 200 tokens.
- transactional/per_token: per-token rates scaled by 1.0x (high fidelity), 0.55x (medium), 0.18x (low-8q).

Discounting and credits

- Error-budget-burn: when a tenant uses >50% of error budget for a billing cycle, offer guided migration suggestions + a one-time credit if switched to a lower fidelity variant by the product team.
- Commitment: dedicated capacity customers can lock session-floor pricing via monthly commit SKU contracts.

Runtime enforcement strategy

- Contracts are evaluated at session creation. Enforcement points:
  - Router: maps incoming requests for a session to the current active variant per fallback_policy.
  - Serving runtime: enforces per-request token caps and telemetry level.
  - Billing pipeline: aggregates session-starts and tokens into invoicing meters.

- Fallback behavior order: preference-based variant routing -> queueing (up to 2s) -> degrade fidelity (quant/variant swap) -> degrade features (disable tool-calls) -> soft-fallback (short response) -> hard-fallback (configured error).

Developer ergonomics (API + SDK examples)

1) Create session (curl example)

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"contract_id":"acme-chat-basic-v1","initial_context":"customer_id:12345"}'

Response: 201 { "session_id": "s-abc123", "expires_at": "2026-12-18T15:04:05Z" }

2) Send message (node SDK sketch)

// pseudocode
const r = await redwood.chat.send({ session_id: 's-abc123', input: 'Hi' });
// r includes tokens_used_this_turn, variant_used, latency_ms

Configuration table (contract -> infra knobs)

| contract_field | runtime_knob | default | implications |
| session_ttl_ms | session_cache_ttl | 1800000 | memory & KV cache retention per session |
| fidelity_budget | session_token_quota | 2000 | early throttle & warning events |
| slo_profile | routing_policy | interactive | priority routing class and preemption |
| telemetry_level | telemetry_sink_config | basic | retention tier and cost center |

Rollout plan (high level)

1) Beta (4 weeks): opt-in customers enable CSCs with telemetry_level= detailed. Run lab with 10 customers across e-commerce, CRM & internal Redwood app.
2) Canary (6 weeks): 20% of new hosted sessions use CSC enforcement engine for routing and billing. Monitor p95 and error budget burn.
3) Gradual ramp (8–12 weeks): increase coverage to 100% for new customers; provide migration tool for existing sessions; prepare dedicated SKU price channels.

Rollout success criteria

- End-to-end p95 for interactive profile remains within 1.2x of baseline.
- No more than 2% of sessions trigger hard-fallback per week.
- Billing pipelines reconcile CSC meters within 12 hours 99% of the time.

Operational runbook (incidents and SRE actions)

1) Symptom: sudden rise in hard-fallbacks for a contract_id.
   - Pager: oncall-routing team.
   - Steps: check router logs -> variant health -> capacity pool status -> scale up or reroute to compatible variant.
   - Temp mitigation: apply emergency override to fallback_policy to promote a stable variant.
2) Symptom: persistent p95 degradation for interactive profile in region eu-west-1.
   - Pager: infra-sre + serving-runtime.
   - Steps: validate traffic spike -> inspect kernel selection logs -> revert recent runtime releases -> enable emergency local prefetching.
3) Symptom: invoicing mismatch for per_session customers.
   - Pager: finance-legal + billing-engineer.
   - Steps: run reconciliation job (billing/reconcile-sessions --contract acme-chat-basic-v1 --window 7d) -> check session-start vs token meter mapping -> escalate to billing pipeline owner.

Observability & telemetry contracts

Minimum telemetry required for published contracts: session_id, contract_id, variant_used, tokens_generated_per_turn, latency_ms, fallback_event. For "detailed" level add token-level traces and user-agent.

Alerting thresholds (recommended)

- p95 breach: alert when p95 exceeds target by 20% for >5 minutes.
- hard-fallback spike: alert when hard-fallback rate >0.5% of sessions in 15 minutes.
- error-budget burn: page when tenant burn reaches 75%.

Security & compliance notes

- All session metadata must be stored according to data-residency settings in the tenant contract.
- Telemetry_level=none still requires hashing of session identifiers for behavioral analytics.

Open questions (product & engineering)

- Should we support multi-tenant shared contracts where multiple customer apps attach to a single contract_id? Pros: simpler pricing. Cons: auditability and error-budget attribution complexity.
- Trade-offs for per_session vs hybrid for very long-running sessions ( > 30k tokens ).
- UX: automatic downgrade prompts to customers vs silent fallback.

Appendix A — Example session contract lifecycle (sequence)

1) Customer calls POST /v1/sessions with contract_id.
2) Router validates contract and assigns session_id.
3) Initial variant selected per fallback_policy.
4) Serving runtime enforces token quota and telemetry level.
5) Billing pipeline consumes aggregated session events.

Appendix B — Example contract change CLI (operator)

# Lock a contract to a new fallback policy
redwood contracts update --contract acme-chat-basic-v1 --set fallback_policy='["gptx-3-8q","gptx-2-8q"]' --author "priya.singh@redwood.ai"

Related pages and references

- See: hosted-to-dedicated-transition-playbook-2026-06-30 for migration considerations.
- See: fidelity-scaling-advisor-product-brief-2026-10-21 for guidance translating fidelity_budget to recommended variants.
